title: Klara and the Sun
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
notes: A poignant, heart-wrenching examination of human connection, grief, and artificial consciousness told through the observant, gentle gaze of an Artificial Friend.

title: If on a winter's night a traveler
author: Italo Calvino
notes: A masterclass in meta-fiction addressing the reader directly. It ignited our deepest debate on the psychological relationship between writer and reader.

title: Drive Your Plow Over the Bones of the Dead
author: Olga Tokarczuk
notes: A subversive noir fairytale centered on an eccentric elder astrologer in a remote Polish village. Dense with William Blake poetry and ecological philosophy.

title: The Master and Margarita
author: Mikhail Bulgakov
notes: Satan arrives in 1930s Soviet Moscow with a mischievous entourage including a giant chess-playing cat. Astonishing satire about art, courage, and censorship.

title: A Gentleman in Moscow
author: Amor Towles
notes: Count Alexander Rostov is sentenced to spend the rest of his life inside the Hotel Metropol. A joyful, wonderfully articulate homage to purpose and hospitality.

title: Piranesi
author: Susanna Clarke
notes: Piranesi lives in the House of infinite rooms and surging ocean tides. An unforgettable celebration of wonder, innocence, and solitary peace.

title: The Dispossessed
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
notes: An ambiguous utopia comparing an anarchist moon colony with a capitalist superpower. One of our club's all-time most quoted texts.
